newsitem.title: FRANCE: French economic crisis hits ad agencies - Seguela.
newsitem.headline: French economic crisis hits ad agencies - Seguela.

text.p: Creative teams in French advertising agencies lack inspiration at present because of France's economic crisis, said Jacques Seguela, vice-chairman of Havas Advertising and a guru of the French advertising industry.
He told Reuters in an interview at the International Advertising Festival in Cannes that his company was looking for new creative talent.
"A country in crisis cannot have a creative spirit," he said, adding that creative teams "were lost in a world in crisis ahead of the dawn of the third millenium."
"You have to go and look for creative talent. Personally I have started to put them on file and go to see them, which is what takes most time," he said on Thursday.

French adverts got a luke-warm reception at the festival earlier in the week, winning a paltry two Lion awards in the billboard poster competition. The advertising film competition is to be judged on Saturday.
France won one silver Lion award and one bronze Lion for its posters, while Brazilian advertisers won 32 Lions, and Britain swept the board with 48 Lions.
"France is a small country which is in the process of looking inward, and is very marked by the crisis," Seguela said.
French creative teams are seeking "a return to basics, the search for a touch of craziness and humour," he said.
To foster creation there should be no forbidden ground in advertising ethics, except for areas affecting children, he said.
"Advertising is children's favourite theatre, it is 30-second stories. So it is appropriate to outlaw pornography, attacks on religion or playing on the theme of death," he said.
Despite France's reputation outside the country for having sexy ads, Seguela said French advertising did not make much explicit use of sexual themes.

But, unlike in Britain or the United States, France has no tradition of public or media outrage against adverts using erotic images or sexually-oriented humour, and there is a greater tolerance of nudity, male or female.

Seguela advised the French Socialist leader, Lionel Jospin, during the recent French parliamentary elections, which led to Jospin's victory, and says he now wants to turn his attention to refashioning the image of the French Communist Party.
The French Communist Party forms part of the new government formed by Socialist leader Lionel Jospin after the left's surprise win in recent parliamentary elections.
"They (the French communists) are people, consumers like anyone else, but they are not managing to communicate on their change," Seguela said. DT/SLA
